baseline.name: PLOS Computational Biology
baseline.scope_notes: Computational methods, software and research delivering substantial biological insight, including genomics and systems biology. Experimental validation is not mandatory; real-world data and reproducibility remain important. Strong conceptual and methodological novelty is required. AI can support research and manuscript development, but ideas, interpretation and accountability remain human; substantive AI use needs tool/use/validation disclosure, while language editing has an exemption. baseline.name: Preventing Chronic Disease
baseline.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
baseline.scope_notes: Chronic-disease prevention and population-health practice, including surveillance/survey and GIS analyses, evaluation and systematic reviews. Scoping reviews are excluded from the systematic-review category. The methods label maps to practical instructional Tools for Public Health Practice articles, which require a one-paragraph summary to the editor before manuscript submission; it does not establish a generic algorithm-paper format. Current guidance says submitted data should be the most current and no older than two years. CDC states that its publications must comply with Executive Orders 14151 and 14168; the editor may discuss identified concerns with the corresponding author. General information: https://www.cdc.gov/pcd/for_authors/general_information.htm.

route.conditions: Ordinary submission/publication has no journal fees under the blanket author-cost policy. Follow article-specific limits and the two-year data-recency policy. Tools for Public Health Practice requires an editor summary before submission and is an instructional methods format. CDC publication and reuse-permission policies apply. No paid membership or editing prerequisite is stated.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None for the ordinary author route. Costs of obtaining permission for chosen third-party material are external and author dependent.
